JUnit tests for org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ExtraFieldUtils.
A ZipExtraField implementation that always throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when parseFromLocalFileData is called, used to verify that ExtraFieldUtils wraps such exceptions in a ZipException.

Header-ID of a ZipExtraField not supported by Commons Compress.

Used to be ZipShort(1) but this is the ID of the Zip64 extra field.
Header-ID of a ZipExtraField not supported by Commons Compress used for the ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsTest.
Number of bytes used to encode a header ID in the extra field wire format.
Number of bytes used to encode the data length in the extra field wire format.
Total overhead in bytes added before each extra field's payload: header-ID (2 bytes) + data-length (2 bytes).
An AsiExtraField configured as a directory with Unix permissions rwxr-xr-x (octal 0755).
An extra field whose header ID is not recognised by Commons Compress.
Combined serialised local-file-data byte array for {@link #asiField} followed by {@link #unrecognizedField}, as it would appear in a ZIP local file header.
Raw local-file-data bytes produced by {@link #asiField}, cached to avoid repeated calls.

Builds the test fixtures:
  • {@link #asiField} – an ASI extra field for a directory with mode 0755
  • {@link #unrecognizedField} – an unrecognised extra field with one data byte
  • {@link #data} – the two fields serialised back-to-back in local-file-data format
Layout: [asiField header (4 bytes)][asiField payload][unrecognizedField header (4 bytes)][unrecognizedField payload]

Verifies that mergeLocalFileDataData and mergeCentralDirectoryData serialise a mix of known and unrecognised extra fields into the correct byte sequences. The central-directory merge uses each field's central-directory length, which may differ from the local-file-data length.

Build expected central-directory byte array. The unrecognized field's central-directory length may differ from its local-file-data length, so we use getCentralDirectoryLength() rather than copying from the local data fixture.
Verifies merge behaviour when the last element is an UnparseableExtraFieldData. Such fields are written without the 4-byte header overhead in both local and central merge.
The unparseable field contributes its raw bytes with no 4-byte header overhead, so the merged result is one byte shorter than the local-data fixture (which has a dummy payload byte).
Build expected central-directory bytes: asiField block followed directly by the unparseable field's central data.
Verifies that parse(byte[]) correctly recognises an AsiExtraField and an UnrecognizedExtraField, and throws an exception when the data is truncated.
Truncate the last byte so the second field's payload is missing.
Verifies that parse(byte[], false) parses extra fields from central-directory data, reporting central-directory lengths rather than local-file-data lengths.
Verifies that an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException thrown by a field's parseFromLocalFileData is wrapped in a ZipException with a message identifying the corrupt field type.
Build a valid byte buffer for the AIOB field so the parse attempt reaches parseFromLocalFileData.
Verifies parse with UnparseableExtraField.READ: valid data yields the normal fields, and truncated data causes the truncated block to be preserved as an UnparseableExtraFieldData.
Truncate the last byte; the second field (header+length only, no payload) becomes unparseable.
The unparseable field stores the 4 raw bytes starting at the second field's position in truncatedData.
Verifies parse with UnparseableExtraField.SKIP: valid data yields the normal fields, and truncated data silently drops the truncated block so only the valid field remains.
With SKIP, the truncated second field is silently discarded.
